summary: An excerpt from a novel (Kate Douglas Wiggin's Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm, though the note does not name the book) at a graduation day. Rebecca and her friend Emma Jane say goodbye as Rebecca anticipates the end of childhood, and Rebecca's class arrives at the church on a flower-decked hayrack drawn by white horses. Adam Ladd, arriving from Portland, watches the procession and then hears a sob from a forlorn girl in white behind a hedge.
one_line: Excerpt from a novel's chapter: Rebecca and Emma Jane part at graduation, and the class arrives at church on a flower-decked hayrack.
key_facts: Rebecca says, "It is coming, Emmie," and recalls Maggie Tulliver closing the golden gates of childhood behind her in The Mill on the Floss.
Emma Jane says she would not care how the gates swung or clanged "if only you and I were on the same side of the gate."
Rebecca tells Emma Jane she is "on the brink" herself and that her only sorrow is that Emma Jane is not graduating with her.
Rebecca asks Emma Jane for a careful hug, "remembering our butter-muslin frailty."
Adam Ladd had just arrived from Portland and was walking to the church when he stopped under a tree in the main street.
The class of which Rebecca was president chose to travel to the church by a decorated hayrack instead of marching two by two.
The hayrack was decked with green vines and bunches of long-stemmed field daisies, and was drawn by two white horses with flower-trimmed reins.
The twelve girls of the class sat in the floral bower on maple boughs, while the ten boys marched on either side wearing buttonhole bouquets of daisies, the class flower.
Rebecca drove the hayrack from a green-covered bench that looked "not unlike a throne."
Adam thought Rebecca, with her tall slenderness, thoughtful brow and fillet of dark braided hair, might have been a young Muse or Sibyl.
Adam recalled the old village street where his mother had walked half a century earlier.
As the crowd turned towards the church, Adam heard a little sob from a forlorn person in white behind a hedge in a nearby garden.
